honourable_mentions.title: Once Upon a Time in Mumbaai

entries.why_it_ranks: One of the most influential Indian crime films ever made. Ram Gopal Varma stripped away glamour and presented the Mumbai underworld with grit, fear and unforgettable characters.
Mani Ratnam and Kamal Haasan created one of Indian cinema's defining gangster epics, balancing crime, power, family and moral decay.
A sprawling crime saga covering generations of revenge, politics and criminal enterprise. Anurag Kashyap created a uniquely Indian gangster universe.
Cold, controlled and frighteningly believable. Ajay Devgn and Vivek Oberoi anchor one of the best films about organized crime and fractured loyalty.
Raw, chaotic and deeply rooted in place. The violence feels less staged than lived, and the final long take is remarkable.
A hard-edged crime investigation that reconstructs the aftermath of the 1993 Mumbai bombings with exceptional intensity and realism.
Begins as a gangster film and slowly becomes something stranger, darker and funnier. Bobby Simha's Assault Sethu is unforgettable.
Sanjay Dutt's Raghu remains one of Hindi cinema's most tragic gangster characters. The film makes crime feel like a downward spiral rather than a fantasy.
A stylish neo-noir with interlocking criminals, betrayal and black humour. Its influence on later Tamil crime cinema is significant.
A powerful crime drama where gang violence is tied to land, caste, displacement and the changing face of Kochi.
Vishal Bhardwaj transforms Macbeth into a Mumbai-underworld tragedy with astonishing performances from Irrfan Khan, Tabu and Pankaj Kapur.
A quiet, modern crime tragedy inspired by Macbeth, with Fahadh Faasil portraying greed and moral collapse with chilling restraint.
A compact neo-noir about betrayal, greed and criminals turning on each other. Sriram Raghavan's control of suspense is excellent.
One of Kannada cinema's strongest modern gangster films, driven by mythic imagery, masculinity, loyalty and inevitable destruction.
Brutal and politically charged, with Ram Gopal Varma exploring faction violence and revenge without softening the ugliness.
A landmark Hindi crime drama that brought darkness, realism and emotional tragedy into mainstream gangster cinema.
Shakespeare's Othello reimagined through crime, caste and political power in rural North India. Ajay Devgn and Saif Ali Khan are exceptional.
A gritty period crime drama where friendship, violence and betrayal unfold with devastating inevitability.
A small theft becomes a fascinating study of morality, police procedure and ordinary people. Fahadh Faasil is superb.
Dhanush's rise from street survivor to gangster is ugly, chaotic and psychologically convincing.
Rashomon-style storytelling gives this coastal crime drama a distinctive structure, atmosphere and cult status.
A harsh, morally complex bandit drama set in Chambal, with outstanding performances and a strong sense of fatalism.
A stylish crime film built around deception, identity and one of Kerala's most notorious fugitives.
What begins with a stolen motorcycle turns into a tense urban crime story, with Dhanush anchoring the escalation convincingly.
A stylish crime caper full of gangsters, mistaken identity and dark humour, with Shahid Kapoor in one of his most memorable early performances.
